summary: Steel lookout in Hardin County on the Shawnee: site materials bought in 1936, photographed 1938, offered for sale 1972, now listed as gone.

facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association list marks the tower as gone; these sources give no removal date and no description of the site.

events.note: In April 1936 purchase of materials was started for a dwelling, garage-woodshed, cistern and latrine at the Peters Creek tower site.
National Archives photograph 'Photograph of Peter's Creek Tower and Improvement' is dated 20 May 1938, so the tower was standing by then.
A listing from about 1942 calls it the Peters Creek Lookout Station, U.S. Forest Service, about 7 miles northwest of Cave-in-Rock, visitors welcome.
Southern Illinoisan advertisement of August 18, 1972 sought bids to sell this and seven other steel lookout towers on the Shawnee National Forest.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NARA record for the 1938 photograph gives its depicted place as Shawnee National Forest (Pope, Illinois), a forest-level label. The lookout listings and the coordinates place the tower in Hardin County, which the record uses.

notes_for_editor: Record checks: county, agency and the 253 m elevation agree with the sources read (Wikidata gives 830 ft). No source gives a build date, a height or a removal date, so no height_m and no built event. Staffing is not stated; the about-1942 listing names a lookout station only, so no staffing key. Access is omitted because no source gives a public or closed status for the site. The photo in the record is the same NARA image (2127993); no new photos. Nothing in these sources describes what remains at the site or whether it can be reached; check Forest Service maps or a site visit before writing more about the site today.
